title: szsdlc project configuration
description: The shape of .szsdlc/config.yml after it has been deep-merged over the shipped defaults. Every entity type, relation, workflow and horizon in szsdlc is data validated by this schema, never code — a project may replace all of it. Unknown keys are rejected everywhere, because a silently ignored key is a configuration that does not do what it says.

version.description: Config format version. Bumped only for a breaking change to this schema.

project.description: Descriptive only. Nothing in the framework branches on these.

paths.description: Where things live, all relative to the project root (the directory containing .szsdlc).

entities.description: Base directory each entity type's `dir` is resolved against.

views.description: Where generated views are written. Every view's `output` is relative to this.

templates.description: Project template overrides. A template not found here falls back to the bundled default.

entity_file.description: Filename holding the frontmatter of a `directory`-layout entity.

id.description: Identifiers are opaque: a type prefix plus a sequential number, and nothing else. Anything embedded that can change or be got wrong invalidates published references.

pattern.description: Format string for a rendered id. Must contain {prefix} and {number}; may contain {key} only when `key` is set.

key.description: Optional project key woven into every id, for projects that share an id space across repos.

padding.description: Zero-padding width for the number. Lookups accept any padding and any case regardless.

parent_relation.description: Which relation name expresses the grouping axis governed by the `can_parent` flag. Named here rather than hardcoded so a project may call it something else.

entity_types.description: Every trackable thing. Keys are snake_case type names used on the command line; each declares its own prefix, storage, workflow and capability flags. Behaviour follows the flags, never the name.

relations.description: Typed edges between entities. Authored on one side only; the inverse is generated and never stored.

roadmaps.description: Horizon buckets of ids — the single home for both ordering and placement. More than one is allowed so a global roadmap can coexist with per-epic ones.

views.description: Generated markdown, written only by `sync`. Never hand-edited.

records.description: The generic mechanism for a project-specific tracked table: a YAML dataset rendered through a template. Empty by default — nothing project-specific ships built in.

standards.description: Conventions matched against an edited path and injected at that moment, rather than preloaded into every session.

tags.description: Tags are free-form and need no declaration; hygiene comes from normalizing at the single write path.

normalize.description: Trim, lowercase, collapse internal whitespace to hyphens, de-duplicate.

validate.description: Thresholds for the warning-level rules. Errors are never configurable.

tag_near_duplicate_distance.description: Two tags within this edit distance are reported as a likely typo (dns vs dsn). 0 disables the rule.

tag_singleton_threshold.description: Once the project has more than this many distinct tags, a tag used exactly once is reported as sprawl. 0 disables the rule.

inbox_stale_days.description: An intake entity sitting in its initial status longer than this is reported — an inbox nobody drains is a graveyard. 0 disables the rule.

identifier.description: snake_case name, typed on the command line.

slug.description: kebab-case name, usable as a filename.

relpath.description: A project-relative POSIX path. Absolute paths and backslashes are rejected so a config is portable across platforms.

prefix.description: The type half of every id of this type. Unique across types.

dir.description: Directory holding this type's entities, relative to paths.entities.

title.description: Human label for views. Defaults to the type name with underscores replaced.

layout.description: `file` for a low-fidelity type — a one-line thought should not cost a directory. `directory` for types that carry artifacts.

intake.description: Accepts typeless capture and appears in the inbox view. Type is discovered by refinement, not asserted at capture.

tracks_progress.description: Has a checkbox artifact parsed for progress.

can_parent.description: Is a legal target of the parent relation.

schedulable.description: May be placed on a roadmap.

persistent.description: A long-lived definition rather than work: never archived when the work around it completes.

fields.description: Extra frontmatter fields beyond the core set (id, title, tags, status, relations).

artifacts.description: Files that may live alongside entity_file in a `directory` entity. Anything else there is an orphan.

progress_artifact.description: The checkbox file counted for progress. Required when tracks_progress is true.

journal_artifact.description: Append-only log written solely by `szsdlc log`.

derived.description: Attributes computed from the relation graph at render time and never written back. Storing them would recreate the stale-state bug this framework exists to remove.

workflow.description: The states this type may hold and the moves between them. A status outside this graph still loads — a hand-edited file must be readable — but `set` refuses to create one.

terminal.description: Work here is finished. Terminal entities leave `next` and the roadmap.

abandoned.description: This terminal status means deliberately given up on rather than completed — the status `drop` moves to. Naming it here is what lets `drop` and `refine` work on a project that renamed its statuses.

requires_artifact.description: Gate checked on ENTERING this state: each named artifact must exist and be non-empty.

requires_tasks_complete.description: Gate checked on ENTERING this state: every checkbox in progress_artifact is ticked.

kind.description: has_incoming: something points here via `relation`. all_incoming_terminal: every such source is terminal (false when there are none). incoming_refs: the list of sources. aggregate_progress: rolled-up progress over the sources.

relation.description: The relation, named as authored. Derivation always walks incoming edges, because the authored side is the one that exists on disk.

inverse.description: Name of the generated back-link. Never authored, never stored.

source_types.description: Types that may author this relation. This doubles as the per-type list of allowed relations — stated once, here.

target_types.description: Types this relation may point at. Omit on the parent relation to derive it from the `can_parent` flags.

cardinality.description: `one` — at most a single target, written as a scalar. `many` — a list.

acyclic.description: Following this relation must never return to its start.

required_on.description: Types for which this relation must be present. A work item with no epic is a finding, not a shrug.

horizons.description: Bucket names in order. `now / next / later` by default, or release names, or dated milestones — the framework does not care.

requires_scheduling.description: type name -> the status at which an entity of that type must appear on this roadmap. Per-roadmap, so a per-epic roadmap can demand nothing while the global one demands everything ready.

template.description: Template path, looked up under paths.templates first and in the bundled defaults second.

schema.description: Optional JSON Schema the dataset is validated against.
